commentary: The liquidity hierarchy divides sharply into three tiers. North American venues dominate: Nasdaq 100 leads decisively with 0.0024% per $1M ILLIQ and 0.8593% AR spread, while NYSE follows with 0.0060% per $1M ILLIQ despite a tighter 0.6638% spread and lower turnover at 0.7209%. The mid-pack comprises Tokyo (0.0343% per $1M ILLIQ, robust 3.1123% turnover), Euronext (0.0303% per $1M ILLIQ, tightest spread at 0.5496%), Hong Kong (0.0362% per $1M ILLIQ), London (0.0803% per $1M ILLIQ), and Xetra (0.0532% per $1M ILLIQ with tight 0.5432% spread). Notably, Xetra shows metric divergence: tight spreads mask middling price-impact costs, suggesting execution challenges despite narrow quoted margins. The laggards—Korea Exchange (0.1586% per $1M ILLIQ, widest 1.5294% spread) and SIX Swiss (0.0460% per $1M ILLIQ but minimal 0.1705% turnover)—reflect structural constraints. Volume concentration remains extreme: Nasdaq's $408.5M comparable volume dwarfs all peers, with the entire European and Asian mid-pack combined below $100M.
